+# Environment
+
+Recorded because most failures encountered in this project were environmental rather
+than properties of the models, and a pinned revision does not by itself reproduce them.
+
+## Execution node
+
+Python 3.12, JDK 21, Ant. OWL-BGP is built from `github.com/iliannakollia/owl-bgp` with
+two edits to its 2015 build file: source and target level 1.5 raised to 8, and the
+removed `-Xlint:all-path` flag dropped. It ships its own HermiT 1.3.8, OWL API 3.4.5 and
+Jena ARQ, so no dependency resolution is required.
+
+The driver holds one JVM per ontology, applies a 60 s per-query timeout and a 300 s load
+budget, and restarts the JVM after a timeout. HermiT does not respond to interruption, so
+a cancelled query keeps running and would otherwise degrade every later query on that
+JVM.
+
+Once that build exists under `tools/owl-bgp`, two scripts prepare the rest:
+
+```
+sh tools/build_runner.sh      # compiles harness/execute/owlbgp/OwlBgpRunner.java
+sh tools/make_owlbgp_cp.sh    # writes tools/owlbgp.cp, which the driver reads
+```
+
+The classpath is a generated file rather than a committed one because it holds absolute
+paths. It names eleven runtime jars; the `-sources`, `-src`, `-tests` and `-test-sources`
+jars that the OWL-BGP distribution also ships are excluded, since a tests jar on the
+classpath can shadow a class.
+
+## GPU node
+
+One NVIDIA H100 (94 GB). Models are served one at a time; the three roster models total
+roughly 180 GB of weights.
+
+| Model | Backend | Constraint |
+|---|---|---|
+| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` | vLLM 0.27.1 | Hybrid Mamba architecture. Cache blocks bound concurrent sequences at 572, below vLLM's default of 1024, so `max_num_seqs` must be lowered. |
+| `google/gemma-4-31B-it` | transformers | vLLM 0.27.1 cannot serve it correctly. Sliding and full attention layers differ in `head_dim` (256 against 512) and key-value heads (16 against 4). The library offers `allow_global_per_layer_attribute_access` to bypass the check; setting it applies one layer's geometry to all layers and mis-serves one layer in six while still producing fluent output. |
+| `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | vLLM 0.27.1 | Served in the publisher's MXFP4 format. |
+
+Decoding is greedy at temperature 0 on both backends, so they implement the same
+decision rule.
+
+## Known traps
+
+`vllm` requires `transformers` v5; v5 is also what raises the per-layer attribute error
+above. Downgrading is not a route around it.
+
+`openai/gpt-oss-120b` ships an `original/` directory holding a 42 GB duplicate of the
+weights in the publisher's own format, which neither backend reads. It reappears whenever
+a tool re-resolves the repository and has twice filled the disk, the second time
+surfacing as a model-loading error rather than a disk error. Fetch with
+`--exclude "original/*" "metal/*"` and serve with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
+
+vLLM's sampler may attempt JIT compilation and fail if no CUDA toolkit is present. Set
+`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` rather than installing one.

+# Probes behind the criterion's own numbers
+
+Three small programs that established properties of query execution reported in the
+article. They are separate from the harness proper because each answers one question
+once, rather than being part of a pipeline, but each produced figures the article
+prints, so they belong with the code rather than in a notebook.
+
+Run them from the repository root; each puts `harness/execute` on the import path
+itself.
+
+| Script | Question | Where the numbers land |
+|---|---|---|
+| `unsat_probe.py` | Does an unsatisfiable class satisfy an arbitrary existential restriction query? | `data/derived/vacuity_probe.json`, the `owl:Nothing` row of the vacuity table |
+| `thing_probe.py` | Is the domain-axiom branch of a lifted query vacuously satisfiable through `owl:Thing`? | the entailed-domain row of the same table |
+| `stability.py` | Is the timeout boundary reproducible across identical runs? | `data/derived/timeout_stability.json`, the reasoner-verdict section |
+
+## What they need
+
+All three drive a reasoner, so they need the JVM and the OWL-BGP build described in
+`docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`, not just the Python environment.
+
+They also read inputs the replication package does not redistribute:
+`unsat_probe.py` and `thing_probe.py` read the prepared African Wildlife Ontology at
+`data/derived/ontologies/awo.owl`, and `stability.py` reads the CQ2SPARQLOWL queries
+under `data/raw/`. Both are produced by `harness/corpus/`, which fetches the sources
+from their origin at the revisions pinned in `data/manifest.json`.
+
+## One caveat on provenance
+
+`unsat_probe.py` and `thing_probe.py` print their results; the JSON they are credited
+with was written from that output by hand rather than by the scripts themselves. The
+row counts in the table can therefore be re-derived by running them and reading the
+output, but not regenerated by re-running a script. `stability.py` writes its JSON
+directly and has no such gap.

+"""How reproducible is the timeout boundary?
+
+Corpus admission excludes queries that time out. If the timeout verdict is not stable
+across identical runs, then the frozen corpus is not reproducible either — a different
+machine, or the same machine on a different day, would admit a different set. Measured
+on swo, the only set where timeouts occur.
+"""
+import sys, json, collections
+sys.path.insert(0, "harness/execute")
+from pathlib import Path
+from engine import add_standard_prologue, ask_to_select, instantiate_placeholders, split_query_file
+from owlbgp_driver import OwlBgpSession
+
+DATA = Path("data/raw/cq2sparqlowl/Data/swo")
+ONT = Path("data/derived/ontologies/swo.owl")
+RUNS = 3
+per_run = []
+for run in range(RUNS):
+    verdicts = {}
+    session = OwlBgpSession(ONT, 60)
+    with session:
+        for p in sorted(DATA.glob("*.rq")):
+            _, raw = split_query_file(p.read_text(errors="replace"))
+            q, _ = instantiate_placeholders(raw)
+            q, _ = ask_to_select(q)
+            q, _ = add_standard_prologue(q)
+            r = session.query(p.stem, q)
+            verdicts[p.stem] = r.status
+            if r.status == "TIMEOUT":
+                session.restart()
+    per_run.append(verdicts)
+    c = collections.Counter(verdicts.values())
+    print(f"run {run+1}: {dict(c)}", flush=True)
+
+keys = sorted(per_run[0])
+unstable = [k for k in keys if len({r[k] for r in per_run}) > 1]
+print(f"\nqueries with a stable verdict across {RUNS} runs: {len(keys)-len(unstable)}/{len(keys)}")
+print(f"UNSTABLE: {len(unstable)}")
+for k in unstable:
+    print(f"  {k}: {[r[k] for r in per_run]}")
+json.dump({"runs": per_run, "unstable": unstable}, open("data/derived/timeout_stability.json","w"), indent=2)

+"""Is the domain-axiom branch of the lifted queries vacuously satisfiable?
+
+Branch (a) is `p rdfs:domain ?c . C rdfs:subClassOf ?c`. Under OWL 2 Direct Semantics
+every property has domain owl:Thing and every class is subsumed by owl:Thing, so ?c may
+bind to owl:Thing whether or not any real domain axiom exists — the top-side twin of the
+owl:Nothing vacuity already filtered at the bottom.
+"""
+import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "harness/execute")
+from pathlib import Path
+from owlbgp_driver import OwlBgpSession
+
+PRE = """PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
+PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>
+PREFIX : <http://www.meteck.org/teaching/ontologies/AfricanWildlifeOntology1.owl#>
+"""
+probes = {
+  "branch (a) for a property with NO domain axiom":
+    "SELECT ?c WHERE { :eats rdfs:domain ?c . :lion rdfs:subClassOf ?c . }",
+  "same, excluding owl:Thing":
+    "SELECT ?c WHERE { :eats rdfs:domain ?c . :lion rdfs:subClassOf ?c . FILTER(?c != owl:Thing) }",
+  "does ?c bind to owl:Thing at all":
+    "SELECT ?c WHERE { :lion rdfs:subClassOf ?c . FILTER(?c = owl:Thing) }",
+}
+with OwlBgpSession(Path("data/derived/ontologies/awo.owl"), 60) as s:
+    for name, q in probes.items():
+        r = s.query("p", PRE + q)
+        print(f"  {name:<48} {r.status:<9} rows={r.rows}")

+"""Does an unsatisfiable class satisfy arbitrary restriction queries under OWL-BGP?
+
+If C is unsatisfiable then C is equivalent to owl:Nothing and C is subsumed by every
+class expression, so C ⊑ ∃p.D holds for every p and D. A generated ontology containing
+one modelling contradiction would then answer CQs it does not cover — and the worst
+ontologies would score best. Verified here rather than assumed.
+"""
+import sys
+sys.path.insert(0, "harness/execute")
+from pathlib import Path
+from rdflib import Graph, Namespace, RDF, RDFS, OWL, URIRef, BNode
+from owlbgp_driver import OwlBgpSession
+
+AWO = Namespace("http://www.meteck.org/teaching/ontologies/AfricanWildlifeOntology1.owl#")
+src = Path("data/derived/ontologies/awo.owl")
+work = Path("/tmp/awo_unsat.owl")
+
+g = Graph(); g.parse(src.as_posix())
+
+# make an unsatisfiable class the honest way: disjoint parents, no explicit owl:Nothing
+ghost = AWO["Ghost"]
+g.add((AWO["plant"], OWL.disjointWith, AWO["animal"]))
+g.add((ghost, RDF.type, OWL.Class))
+g.add((ghost, RDFS.subClassOf, AWO["plant"]))
+g.add((ghost, RDFS.subClassOf, AWO["animal"]))
+g.serialize(work.as_posix(), format="xml")
+print(f"built {work} with an unsatisfiable class :Ghost (plant AND animal, disjoint)")
+
+PRE = f"""PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
+PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>
+PREFIX : <{AWO}>
+"""
+# :eats never relates Ghost to anything in the asserted ontology
+probes = {
+  "Ghost has SOME eats-restriction (should be vacuous)":
+    "SELECT ?f WHERE { :Ghost rdfs:subClassOf [ a owl:Restriction ; owl:onProperty :eats ; owl:someValuesFrom ?f ] . }",
+  "Ghost subsumed by an invented class":
+    "SELECT ?x WHERE { :Ghost rdfs:subClassOf ?x . }",
+  "owl:Nothing has an eats-restriction":
+    "SELECT ?f WHERE { owl:Nothing rdfs:subClassOf [ a owl:Restriction ; owl:onProperty :eats ; owl:someValuesFrom ?f ] . }",
+  "ANY class with an eats-restriction (does Ghost pollute?)":
+    "SELECT ?c WHERE { ?c rdfs:subClassOf [ a owl:Restriction ; owl:onProperty :eats ; owl:someValuesFrom ?f ] . }",
+}
+for label, path in [("clean awo", src), ("awo + unsat Ghost", work)]:
+    print(f"\n--- {label} ---")
+    with OwlBgpSession(path, 60) as s:
+        for name, q in probes.items():
+            r = s.query("p", PRE + q)
+            print(f"  {name:<52} {r.status:<9} rows={r.rows}")

+#!/usr/bin/env sh
+# Compile the OWL-BGP batch runner into tools/runner.
+#
+# The runner is one class that holds a reasoner open and streams queries through it. Its
+# source lives with the rest of the harness, in harness/execute/owlbgp; only the build
+# output belongs under tools, beside the OWL-BGP build it links against.
+#
+# Usage: sh tools/build_runner.sh
+set -eu
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+bgp="$root/tools/owl-bgp"
+[ -d "$bgp" ] || { echo "missing $bgp - see docs/ENVIRONMENT.md" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+cp_value="$bgp/build/classes"
+for jar in "$bgp"/lib/*.jar; do
+  case "$jar" in *-sources.jar|*-tests.jar|*-test-sources.jar|*-src.jar) continue ;; esac
+  cp_value="$cp_value:$jar"
+done
+
+mkdir -p "$root/tools/runner"
+javac -cp "$cp_value" -d "$root/tools/runner" \
+      "$root/harness/execute/owlbgp/OwlBgpRunner.java"
+echo "built tools/runner"

+#!/usr/bin/env sh
+# Write tools/owlbgp.cp for this checkout.
+#
+# The driver reads the classpath from a file rather than assembling it, because the jar
+# set is part of what a verdict depends on and belongs in one auditable place. The file
+# holds absolute paths, so it is generated per machine instead of being committed.
+#
+# The lib directory also ships -sources, -src, -tests and -test-sources jars. They are excluded:
+# the runs that produced the recorded verdicts used the eleven runtime jars only, and a
+# tests jar on the classpath can shadow a class.
+#
+# Usage: sh tools/make_owlbgp_cp.sh
+set -eu
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
+bgp="$root/tools/owl-bgp"
+[ -d "$bgp" ] || { echo "missing $bgp - see docs/ENVIRONMENT.md" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+cp_value="$root/tools/runner:$bgp/build/classes"
+n=0
+for jar in "$bgp"/lib/*.jar; do
+  case "$jar" in
+    *-sources.jar|*-tests.jar|*-test-sources.jar|*-src.jar) continue ;;
+  esac
+  cp_value="$cp_value:$jar"
+  n=$((n + 1))
+done
+printf '%s:\n' "$cp_value" > "$root/tools/owlbgp.cp"
+echo "wrote tools/owlbgp.cp ($n runtime jars)"
